mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome to this journey, where curiosity hums just beneath the surface of everything we do. Have you ever found yourself wondering about the quirky rituals and habits that shape our daily lives—those little things we barely notice, until someone holds them up to the light? Together, we’re about to dive into a world where the line between high culture and pop culture gets a little fuzzy, and where the ordinary suddenly feels anything but. Through the sharp and playful lens of David Foster Wallace, in his collection A Supposedly Fun Thing I'll Never Do Again, we’ll explore everything from the bizarre allure of luxury cruises to the intense world of junior tennis, and even the chaotic energy of state fairs. Wallace’s essays invite us to look at pleasure, entertainment, and meaning in ways that are funny, thoughtful, and sometimes a bit skeptical—but always deeply human. As we move through these stories, you’ll notice how the familiar can become wonderfully strange, and how even the strangest moments reveal something profound about who we are. Wallace’s voice—both wry and tender—guides us through the maze of late twentieth-century America, making us pause and reflect on what it means to seek fun, meaning, and authenticity in a world obsessed with spectacle. So, as we peel back the layers of everyday life, get ready to discover the surprising patterns that shape our experiences. Let’s explore together, and see what we might find beneath the surface—not just about the world around us, but about ourselves, too.
